name: {{dow}} Cloud Impact Levels
purpose: How sensitive the information is that a cloud service may hold for the {{dow.current}}.
what: Four levels in use: IL2, IL4, IL5 and IL6. IL2 is for public and other non-controlled information, IL4 for controlled unclassified information, IL6 for classified information up to SECRET. IL5 changed in 2025.

binds.line: The DFARS lets a cloud contract go only to a provider that DISA has granted a provisional authorization at the level the work needs.

verifiedBy.line: DISA grants the provisional authorization. The mission owner’s authorizing official still grants the authorization to operate.

sits.line: Layer 5. The levels were built on FedRAMP baselines plus the department’s own controls. Neither side has yet said how they line up with FedRAMP’s new classes.

sources.title: Department of Defense Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. This is the last single-volume guide that could be opened, and it is not the current edition. It gives the four levels in use (level 1 was merged into IL2 and level 3 into IL4), IL2 as non-controlled unclassified information, IL4 as controlled unclassified information, IL6 as classified information up to SECRET, and the provisional authorization as approved by the DISA authorizing official while the mission owner grants the authorization to operate.

sources.title: July 2025 Maintenance Release: STIGs to Be Released

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. For the Cloud Service Provider SRG, Version 1, Release 3: ‘Updated guidance for approach for IL4 addressing both Moderate and High categorizations. IL5 now accommodates unclassified National Security System/National Security Information with CUI no longer part of this Impact Level.’ The guide itself had by then been split into a Cloud Service Provider SRG and mission owner documents.

sources.title: Cloud Service Provider Security Requirements Guide, current release

verification.note: The current release could not be opened on 14 November 2026: the document library’s list did not load for a script, and the 2026 release notes sit on a host whose certificate was not trusted. Tried: https://www.cyber.mil/dccs/dccs-documents/ and https://www.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads. DISA’s Cloud Connection Process Guide of December 2025 cites an edition of September 2025. So this card’s wording for IL4 and IL5 rests on the 2025 release notes, not on the current text.

Read on 14 November 2026: the contracting officer ‘shall only award a contract to acquire cloud computing services from a cloud service provider’ that ‘has been granted provisional authorization by Defense Information Systems Agency, at the level appropriate to the requirement’. The clause DFARS 252.239-7010 carries the guide into the contract.

terms.line: A work of the United States government. This round shows the card, in Lensatic’s own words, and says where its wording rests on release notes.

related.line: Each level was defined on top of a FedRAMP baseline.
The mission owner’s authorization to operate is an RMF decision.
